title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): work in the presheaf topos of functors on k-algebras, with the ring object O_k given by A ↦ A. For a k-module M, V(M)(A) = Hom_k(M,A) = Hom_A(M_A, A). This functor is represented by Sym^*(M). By Yoneda, morphisms V(N) → V(M) correspond to k-linear maps u: M → Sym^*(N). Write u = Σ u_i with u_i: M → Sym^i(N), a locally finite family.

This page:
(1) Explicit formula. For x* ∈ V(N)(A) = Hom_k(N,A), let x̃*: Sym N → A be the canonical k-algebra extension. Then u*(x*) = x̃* ∘ u ∈ Hom_k(M,A), so u*(x*)(x) = Σ_i x̃*^i(u_i(x)), where x̃*^i is the restriction of x̃* to Sym^i N.
(2) Effect of scaling. Replacing x* by λx* (λ ∈ A) multiplies x̃*^i by λ^i. So composing with the homothety λ on V(N) corresponds to the operation u = Σ u_i ↦ u^λ = Σ λ^i u_i.
(3) Conclusion. u* is homogeneous of degree n, meaning u* ∘ λ_{V(N)} = λ^n_{V(M)} ∘ u* for all A and λ, if and only if u_i = 0 for every i ≠ n, i.e. u is a linear map M → Sym^n N.
(4) Proof. Take the universal case A = k[T], λ = T. This gives Σ (T^i − T^n) u_i(x) = 0 in Sym(N)[T]. Comparing coefficients gives u_i(x) = 0 for i ≠ n.

The next page deduces that degree-1 homogeneous morphisms are exactly the linear maps M → N, hence that V is fully faithful (contravariantly). It then extends the analysis to products Π V(N_α) = V(⊕ N_α) via multidegrees.

Purpose: this is foundational set-up for the 'yoga coalgèbres ↦ Algèbres' annex of the divided-power de Rham notes. Its role is to identify functorial polynomial operations between linear functors with maps into symmetric powers, presumably to be dualised later into divided powers / coalgebra structures.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor notational slips: 'O_K' should be O_k, and the homothety is on V(N) (i.e. on N_A); the scribbled text mixes M_A and N_A before correcting.
On the next page, '(comme n arbitraire)' should really be 'i ≠ n arbitrary'. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Morphisms of affine-space functors V(N) → V(M) correspond to linear maps M → Sym^* N (Yoneda plus representability by Sym).
ideas.modern_name: Vector bundle / affine space functor W(M)^∨, Yoneda for representable functors

ideas.what: Homogeneity of degree n of a functorial morphism detected via the universal scalar T in k[T]; homogeneous degree-n morphisms correspond to maps into Sym^n.
ideas.modern_name: Homogeneous polynomial laws / G_m-equivariance (grading via G_m-action)
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (polynomial laws, 1963); SGA 3 (gradings as G_m-actions)

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of V via the degree-1 morphisms (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of M ↦ V(M) as O-modules

deep.surprise_reason: Entirely standard foundational material (Yoneda for vector-bundle functors, homogeneity via G_m-scaling), as in SGA 3 and Demazure–Gabriel. Its only interest is as a preliminary to the divided-power coalgebra annex.
transcription_corrections: The struck passage reads roughly 'la multiplication ~ composition de x* avec une homothétie λ_(M_A) (λ∈A)', corrected to 'λ dans le O_k-module (resp. N le O_A-module N_A)'.
The correction 'la restr.' is written above the struck word 'extension'/'la' in the gloss on x̃*^i: the restriction of x̃* to Sym^i N.
